virF is a transcriptional activaor that is required for virulence and is related to the AraC regulator.
virF encocdes a transcriptional activaor controlling the yop gene expression and that this activator is related to AraC.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of virF, the first regulatory gene identified in the yersinia pathogenicity island, which is the counterpart in virulent yersinias of the chromosomal genes of E. coli involved in virulence.
the regulation of virulence in pathogenic Yersinia.
the characterization of virF, a gene which encodes a transcription regulator controlling the production of virulence factors in virulent yersinias.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the virF gene product is a transcriptional activators which is responsible for the calcium dependency phenotype of virulent Yersinia.
the virF gene product is a transcriptional activators that controls the expression of vir genes in response to a change in temperature, independently of the presence or absence of calcium ions.
the virF product is an AraC-related protein which is responsible for the thermodependence of Yop secretion in Yersinia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
virF, a transcriptional activators, is the master switch controlling the expression of Yops.
virF is a positive regulator of the vir regulon and that its activity is not calcium dependent.
virF is the key element in the control of the virulence of yersiniae.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of virulence genes in yersiniae has a lot in common with the regulation of the arabinose operone in E. coli.
the virulence of Yersinia is controlled by a single transcriptional regulator, VirF, which is homologous to AraC.
virF is the first example of a transcriptional activators of a bacterial virulence regulon.
